question:
What is the value of the following expression?

\[\frac{100^2 - 7^2}{70^2 - 11^2} \cdot \frac{(70 - 11)(70 + 11)}{(100 - 7)(100 + 7)}\]
solution:
Each difference of squares matches a product in the second fraction, so factoring will reveal reciprocal fractions.

Using \(u^2-v^2=(u-v)(u+v)\), the expression becomes
\[
\frac{(100-7)(100+7)}{(70-11)(70+11)}
\cdot
\frac{(70-11)(70+11)}{(100-7)(100+7)}.
\]
Every factor is positive, so all the common factors can be canceled. The two fractions are reciprocals, and their product is \(\boxed{1}\), choice \(\textbf{A}\).
